notes: All three assigned rows supply the same broad emotional-eating/disordered-eating description and p.4 locator, without an outcome, predictor, contrast, hypothesis, or test identifier. Page 4 contains LCA selection, demographic logistic regressions and multiple outcome Wald tests. Row order and numeric matching cannot identify the assigned target. Candidate outcome tests (pp.4–6, section 3.5/Table 4; printed approximate chi-square/Wald tests, not converted effects): NIAS total 16.11, p < .001; NIAS Fear 3.66, p not printed; NIAS Picky Eating 4.28, p not printed; NIAS Appetite 29.88, p < .001 from Table 4 three-star legend; CIA psychosocial impairment 32.26, p < .001; EAT-26 disordered eating 4.71, p not printed (no star; no bound inferred); stress 36.12, p < .001; anxiety 33.22, p < .001; depression 14.24, p < .01; psychological flexibility 37.74, p < .001. Other candidates: LCA model-fit tests (section 3.2/Table 2) and demographic odds ratios (section 3.4/Table 3); no target is selected. Candidate common outcome/LCA sample: 533 participants; explicit final mutually exclusive classes sum 98 + 97 + 190 + 148 = 533. Recruitment 731; excluded 198 for failing more than one attention/validity check or completing surveys in under 30 minutes. Section 2.4 reports <5% missing per outcome handled by grand mean substitution. Table 3 excludes one participant without woman/man gender classification; candidate demographic regression participant count would be 533 - 1 = 532, conditional on no further exclusions (not independently assigned as analytic N). Because the critical test remains unidentified, no candidate N is written to the core value. Authors report overall replication/extension and support for the four-class hypothesis, but explicitly state that the weight/shape disordered-eating hypothesis was contradicted. Without row-specific outcome correspondence, neither an overall successful verdict nor a failed outcome verdict can be assigned to this row; a mixed label would synthesize across unspecified targets. PDF pp.4–6 rendered and visually inspected. All values remain null because test correspondence is unresolved; status done denotes completed source review. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not a claim about original-source availability.
